title: findings@10
description: Successor to findings@9, the CLUSTER document declared on the reconcile steps and on the review/design-qa steps that feed one, including review steps in workflows with no reconcile stage. Identical to findings@9 in every constraint — same `required: ["severity"]`, same `severity` and `open_severity` ladders and declared order, same optional `id`/`open_severity`/`members`/`held`/`demoted_from`/`operator_resolved`/`prior_disposition`, `additionalProperties` stays true. The only change is prose: several field descriptions were stale against the corpus that now consumes this document. The engine enforces byte-identity on a frozen registration, so even a prose-only correction lands as a fresh version rather than an in-place edit. findings@9 stays registered for runs that already declared it; it is now orphaned once every workflow in the corpus repoints here.

id.description: Stable identifier for the finding or cluster, unique within the payload. Not `required`: the builtin `aggregate` carries through only the input element's own keys, so a schema requiring `id` would make aggregate's pass-through payloads unregisterable.

severity.description: The finding's severity, on 02 §6's five-value ladder. The enum's document order IS the order thresholds compare on (`any(severity >= high)`) and the order `aggregate` reduces over: info < low < medium < high < blocker. Judges author on the general or security ladder fragment and map onto these values at emit time.

open_severity.description: The cluster's severity WHILE IT REMAINS OPEN, as a scalar on the same five-value ladder as `severity` (max of the member severities for a multi-member cluster). Present ONLY on a cluster with no settling prior_disposition ruling; omitted on settled ground, so `any(open_severity >= high)` reads the open set and nothing else. Emitted by synthesize-findings and carried through `aggregate` verbatim like every non-severity key.

file.description: Repo-relative path the finding is anchored to.

line.description: 1-indexed line within `file`. Optional per 02 §6. An explicit `null` is ALSO valid — synthesize-findings emits `line: null` for a finding whose scope is the whole file or the whole commit, where there is no single line to anchor to; that is distinct from simply omitting the key. `minimum` applies only when the value is a number, so the integer case stays constrained and null passes untouched.

evidence.description: What a skeptic can re-run or re-read to confirm the finding.

alternative.description: A concrete alternative to the flagged approach. OPTIONAL at every severity: the judge-design rule pairing a blocker with an alternative is a prose obligation in that contract, and synthesize-findings — which emits this same payload and adds no alternative — would be refused by a schema-level conditional.

members.description: The cluster's member severities, in arrival order. Present on the `aggregate` output ONLY. It is NOT how synthesize-findings carries a cluster: synthesize declares `payload = "findings-cluster@3"`, whose scalar-or-array `severity` is the `aggregate` builtin's INPUT contract, reading member severities from each input element's own `severity` field rather than from a `members` array; the linkage between elements of one cluster is carried in `member_ids` (findings-cluster@3), not here. Values are the same ladder as `severity`; the constraint is not repeated as an `enum` here because `aggregate@1` leaves `members` unconstrained and the conjunction of the two documents must stay satisfiable.

held.description: Set by the builtin `aggregate` (06 §2): the cluster's spread reached `hold_spread`, so it is excluded from automatic routing and materializes a `<step>-held` human step. Absent on any step whose `aggregate` declares no `hold_spread`, since a hold can never trigger there.

demoted_from.description: Set by `aggregate` when the computed value sits below the cluster's maximum member — the recorded demotion trail (02 §6). Absent when nothing was demoted, which today means absent everywhere: every aggregate step in the corpus declares `method = "max"`, and max never computes below its own maximum member. It stays declared so the trail keeps one meaning and stays pinned to the five-value ladder wherever one does appear — carried forward on a cluster an earlier, reducing method produced, or emitted again if a workflow ever reduces by anything other than max. `additionalProperties` is true, so dropping the declaration would leave the key unchecked rather than refused.

operator_resolved.description: Set when an operator accepted a held cluster's value via `docket step approve|reject`; thresholds re-apply over the resolved set (02 §6). It records that THIS round's hold was decided, and does not survive into a later round — `prior_disposition` is what carries a decision forward.

prior_disposition.description: How this same locus was already ruled on in an EARLIER fix-loop round. Set by synthesize-findings when its inputs identify a cluster as a re-occurrence, and carried through unchanged by `aggregate`. Its presence is the signal that the cluster is settled ground rather than a discovery: a reader — human or panel — owes it a re-read of the earlier ruling before spending a second decision. Absent on a genuinely new cluster, which is the ordinary case. Every sub-field is optional so a partially-known disposition is still recordable; an empty object records nothing and is no better than omitting the field. A re-review round's payload spans the STANDING SET, not the delta: a finding still open is carried forward with this key set even when it did not re-occur in that round's inputs, emitted as one element carrying the scalar the previous aggregate reduced it to rather than its original member array — spread 0, so `hold_spread` cannot re-hold ground an operator already ruled on. Clustering only the delta dropped 24 open findings, nine of them high, out of every later aggregate in a run that hit this exact gap.

round.description: The fix-loop round the ruling was made in, 0-based — round 0 is the first review, before any fix step ran.

ruling.description: What was decided, in the decider's terms. Conventional forms: `accepted` (the computed value stood), `corrected-to-<severity>` (approved with `--value`), `rejected`, or `deferred` (accepted on the promise of later work, which `follow_up_issue` must then name).

ruled_by.description: Who decided: `operator`, or `panel <proposal-id>` where a tribunal did. A ruling with no name is not a ruling anyone can re-read.

follow_up_issue.description: The issue id the deferred work was filed as. REQUIRED IN PRACTICE when `ruling` is a deferral: a deferral with no issue is the evaporation this field exists to make visible (a past run had two approved hold remedies, no next round, and no issue anywhere in the store). Not schema-required, because a schema-level conditional here would refuse payloads the aggregate legitimately carries through.
